business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Remarketing of Secondhand Hydraulic Earthmovers and Rollers

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-Germany Double Taxation Agreement (1959, as amended)
France-China Double Taxation Agreement (amended by 2013 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-1 et seq., L.561-2-2, and L.561-45-1; Ordonnance n° 2020-115 of 4 February 2020 reinforcing the national AML/CFT framework; Décret n° 2021-162 of 12 February 2021; Code de commerce, Articles L.123-2-1 and R.123-223 (register of beneficial owners / registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); EU Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5th AML Directive).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of proposed ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or consular office in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing for corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in shareholder jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French translation of corporate documents of shareholder
Power of attorney for incorporation agent

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the UN Security Council consolidated list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, UK HM Treasury sanctions list, and the French Tracfin 'Alerte' database. Screening of all UBOs, directors, signatories, and senior trading personnel; adverse media screening in French and English; enhanced due diligence for PEPs, requiring documented source of wealth and source of funds. Re-screening at least every six months or upon any material event. For ISIC 4659 used earthmovers, any trade-based money laundering indicator must be reported to Tracfin as a suspicious transaction report (STR).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet des formalités entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) — RCS via Infogreffe screen for naming conflicts.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SAS may use a French or foreign-language name; if written in non-Latin characters, a mandatory French/Latin-alphabet transliteration must be included in the electronic filing. The name must be lawful, non-misleading, and not contrary to public policy or protected business name rights. Terms suggesting regulated activity (banking, insurance, finance, legal, etc.) require prior licensing or ministerial clearance and are prohibited without such approval.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Fonds de pension, gestion de portefeuille
Française, Nationale, République, Paris (when misleading or implying state patronage)
Groupement, holding, or financial terms requiring special justification
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not provide a formal name-reservation window. If the registration filing is rejected for a naming conflict, file a formal 'recours gracieux' with the Greffe du tribunal de commerce within two months of notification, attaching evidence of prior use or distinctiveness. If the Greffe maintains the refusal, file a 'recours hiérarchique' to the President of the Tribunal de commerce in référé proceedings. The commercial registry may also be compelled through the court's summary jurisdiction. Alternatively, the person incorporating may re-file with a new distinct name after verifying availability on Infogreffe.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible under French law through an approved 'société de domiciliation' holding a préfectoral agrément, provided a written domiciliation agreement is executed. A mere postal box is not accepted as a registered office. For a used heavy-machinery trading SAS, operating substance is enhanced by maintaining a separate logistics/warehouse address and retaining transport and customs documentation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: ~45% probability over a 12-month period for a wholesale second-hand machinery trader; tax authorities and customs may conduct unannounced on-site inspections, requiring proof of physical presence, inventory records, and transaction trail.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark fixed fee (€1,100–€2,000 excl. VAT)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff set by Décret n° 2016-230

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Code de commerce, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-28 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); Article R.123-1 et seq. (RCS registration); Article 1835 et seq. of the Civil Code (general contract provisions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court), acting as the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) filing agency.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de la Société (Articles of Association) and, where applicable, a formal incorporation filing via the M0 (or M0-SAS) form to the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for SAS; however, if share capital is set, it must be fully subscribed and the contribution must be either fully paid in cash (for cash contributions) or delivered in kind (for contributions in kind) prior to incorporation, with funds deposited in a designated escrow account (blocage de fonds) with a bank or notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the undersigned subscribers hereby approve and adopt the draft Statuts of the Société par Actions Simplifiée and subscribe in full to the share capital as detailed in the subscription list; (2) That the registered office is fixed at the address specified in the Statuts, and that the President may rent, equip, and manage such premises as necessary to carry out the corporate purpose; (3) That the individuals named in the extract of the deliberations are appointed as President and General Management (Directeur Général) for the legal term, with full powers to represent the company; (4) That all pre-incorporation acts are ratified; (5) That the President is authorized to complete the registration and publication formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Company Name and Availability Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) and the RCS via the Infogreffe legal forms portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability check on the INPI databases and ensure the proposed corporate name does not conflict with existing registered trademarks or corporate denominations. Submit an online inquiry to reserve the name for a temporary period; receive a positive result before proceeding with drafting the statutes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or collides with an existing right, select a differentiated name and re-file; any third-party opposition may be resolved by obtaining a prior trademark coexistence consent or selecting a new denomination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Notarization, and Execution of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private legal practitioner (lawyer) or notary (notaire) responsible for authenticating status; execution before the parties
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a corporate attorney to draft the Statuts in accordance with the mandatory SAS provisions, setting out the corporate purpose (including wholesale trading of used construction excavators), share capital details, board composition, and President appointment. The Statuts may be signed under private signature or by notarial act if the company acquires real estate or contributes property. Each subscriber signs the document containing the exact shares subscribed and the amount of capital paid.
required_dossiers: Subscriber identification passports or NIE cards
Capital contribution proof (bank certificate in lieu of escrow or deposit certificate)
Business plan (if required by the introductory advisor)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarial authentication is needed and delays occur, switch to a private signature version; any statutory defects may be cured by amending the Statuts and re-executing with all parties, then filing the rectified document.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Share Capital into a Blocked Account and Issuance of a Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank or notary in France acting as escrow agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary bank account in the name of the company in formation. Transfer the full amount of cash capital (no minimum but must equal stated capital) into the account. Obtain an attestation de dépôt de fonds (funds deposit certificate) from the bank or notary; this certificate is loss-free evidence required for the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Passport of the President and statutory agent
Proof of address of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the deposit, use a regulated mutual credit institution or notary escrow; any shortfall in capital can be remedied by a supplementary cash deposit and reissuance of the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Incorporation Notice (Avis de Constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal announcement journal (journal d'annonces légales) approved for the commercial court district
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft a legal notice containing the company’s trading name, form (SAS), registered office address, corporate purpose, share capital, name and address of the President, and the RCS registry where the company will be registered. Publish the notice in an approved legal gazette; the advertisement must appear before the RCS filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette publication is defective, reissue a corrected publication within the statutory timeline; the date of the valid notice will be used for the legal opposition period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the M0 Incorporation File to the RCS (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Court Registry) – RCS desk, or online via the Infogreffe or formalities portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the full incorporation file, including the Statuts, the M0 form (déclaration de création d’entreprise), bank deposit certificate, legal announcement receipt, identity documents of the directors, the registered office accommodation certificate (attestation de domiciliation), and proof of payment of the filing fee. The registry will check the file and issue the Extrait Kbis within the processing period.
required_dossiers: Civil liability insurance or banking details (if required)
Identity and nationality proof of the President and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query (demande de complément), the legal representative must submit the requested corrections or missing documents within the specified deadline (usually 30 days); failure to comply leads to termination of the filing, after which a fresh file must be submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Officers and Post-Registration Governance Actions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting (or adopt a written unanimous first decision) formally approving the incorporation, ratifying the Statuts, appointing the President and any other officers, adopting the registered office address, and authorizing the signature opening procedures. File the nomination of the President and any changes to the RCS if not already included in the M0 form.
required_dossiers: First board meeting minutes (or written decision)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the officer filing, correct the forms and resubmit; any irregularity in the disposition of the corporate governance can be ratified by a new unanimous decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Corporate Tax and Administrative Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF, Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), and the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (CFE) / Infogreffe platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Extrait Kbis and then request the SIRET number, VAT (Europa-TVA) number, and corporate tax account. Register with social security for the President (auto-entrepreneur or assimilé salarié status depending on scheme). Open a corporate bank account with a licensed French bank and file the beneficial ownership declaration (bénéficiaires effectifs).
required_dossiers: Identities and addresses of directors and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registration attracts penalties; remedy by using the online solidary platform to obtain retroactive certificates if administrative delay is proven and by paying any moderate late fees promptly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale des Entreprises (DGE) – Ministerial Industry Licensing; however, no specific industrial operating license applies to the trading and remarketing of used construction machinery under ISIC 4659.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable (no dedicated operating license for wholesale used earthmoving machinery trading); the business operates solely under the company's RCS registration and Kbis extract.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Exempt (activity is a wholesale trader; no manufacturing, surface processing, or disposal operations requiring full EIA).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not directly applicable to an office-based wholesaler; should storage or light assembly of machinery occur, compliance with waste handling rules (Décret n°2005-635, hazardous waste tracking), wastewater discharge standards (Article R.213-48 et seq. of the Code de l'environnement), and VOC emission limits (Directive 2010/75/EU, Code de l'environnement) will be required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local fire department (commission de sécurité) if premises host any public-access or storage capacity above thresholds; structural load inspections for any warehouse space used to store heavy earthmoving equipment; and workplace health and safety registration with service de prévention et de santé au travail (SPST) for any employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), administered through the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the official tax portal impots.gouv.fr. Customs registrations and export formalities are administered by the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects (DGDDI) through the French customs portal douane.gouv.fr. The European Union VAT identification number is issued and administered by the DGFiP.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is incorporated through the guichet unique operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI). The registration process results in allocation of a SIREN number for the legal entity, a SIRET number for each establishment, and an APE activity code. The company must submit its tax information and business commencement details to the competent SIE through the applicable registration and activity forms. Where the company carries out transactions giving rise to French VAT liability, it must request a French VAT identification number from the SIE. The VAT number generally uses the format FR plus a two-digit validation key and the nine-digit SIREN number. A non-established foreign entity must register with the designated French foreign-business tax service or competent SIE where it is liable for French VAT and cannot rely on a reverse-charge rule. A non-EU entity generally must appoint a French fiscal representative unless an applicable legal or treaty exemption applies. An EORI number must be obtained from French customs for customs clearance, import, export, or other customs activity. VIES validation should be completed for intra-EU transactions. Registration does not itself determine VAT liability; the place-of-supply, importation, domestic supply, export, and reverse-charge rules must be tested transaction by transaction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SAS is subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, or IS) by default. A qualifying SAS may elect temporarily for income tax treatment (impôt sur le revenu, or IR) if statutory conditions are met, including conditions relating to business activity, ownership, employee headcount, turnover or balance-sheet size, age of the company, and ownership by individuals or qualifying entities. The election is generally limited to five fiscal years and is subject to notification deadlines; it is not an unrestricted United States-style check-the-box election. A qualifying SAS may also be treated as a société de personnes in limited circumstances where statutory conditions are satisfied. France has no general domestic check-the-box regime. French anti-hybrid mismatch rules implement the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive requirements and can deny deductions, impose inclusion, or restrict relief where hybrid instruments, hybrid entities, imported mismatches, or branch mismatches produce a non-taxation outcome. These rules do not create a general elective entity-classification regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or VAT), supplemented by customs duties and import VAT administered under French and European Union customs and VAT legislation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For the French VAT franchise regime applicable to commercial activities, the principal annual turnover threshold is EUR 85,000, with a tolerance threshold of EUR 93,500 under the applicable statutory conditions. The principal thresholds for services are EUR 37,500 and EUR 41,250. These thresholds concern eligibility for the franchise en base and are not a universal safe harbor for non-established businesses. A foreign business may be required to register from the first taxable transaction in France where no domestic reverse charge, distance-selling simplification, or other special regime applies. Intra-EU distance sales are generally subject to the EUR 10,000 Union-wide threshold, subject to the One Stop Shop regime. Import VAT is not subject to the domestic turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting through registered private platforms (plateformes de dématérialisation partenaires, or PDPs), with the public portal PPF serving principally as a directory and reporting infrastructure under the revised implementation framework. From 1 September 2026, all French businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices; large and mid-sized businesses must issue domestic B2B electronic invoices from that date. Small and micro-enterprises must generally issue domestic B2B electronic invoices from 1 September 2027. Electronic reporting of relevant B2C and cross-border transactions is phased in with the same implementation timetable. The system uses structured or hybrid invoice formats and mandatory data fields, including transaction, payment, VAT, and party information as applicable. France does not generally require real-time pre-clearance of every invoice before issuance. Invoices to French public-sector entities are submitted through Chorus Pro. Until the applicable mandate date, ordinary French invoice, record-retention, authenticity, integrity, and legibility requirements remain applicable. Used construction machinery transactions may require specific VAT treatment, including margin-scheme analysis for qualifying second-hand goods and reverse-charge analysis for qualifying cross-border or domestic transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to a destination outside the European Union may be exempt from French VAT with the right to deduct input VAT where the supplier, the supplier's customs representative, or an authorized intermediary can substantiate that the goods physically left the EU customs territory and that the statutory export conditions were met. The export declaration must identify the transaction and the customs exit must be confirmed electronically through the customs export control system. The seller must retain the commercial invoice, transport evidence, export declaration data, exit confirmation, and accounting records linking the goods to the invoice. Intra-EU supplies of goods may qualify for the zero-rate exemption where the customer is VAT-identified in another Member State, the goods are dispatched or transported to that Member State, the supplier reports the transaction correctly, and the supplier retains transport evidence. Services are not automatically zero-rated merely because the customer is offshore. Their treatment depends on the place-of-supply rules, customer status, use-and-enjoyment provisions, and any applicable exemption. The margin scheme for qualifying second-hand goods generally does not provide a conventional recoverable-input-VAT export profile; the resale status and acquisition history must be documented before applying any export or margin treatment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice identifying the seller, purchaser, goods, values, VAT treatment, and transaction terms

Electronic export declaration submitted through the EU customs system, including the correct commodity code, customs procedure, customs value, origin information where required, and exporter or representative details
Master Reference Number or equivalent export declaration reference
Electronic confirmation that the goods exited the EU customs territory, including the exit results or exit accompanying record
Transport evidence appropriate to the route, such as bill of lading, sea waybill, CMR consignment note, air waybill, rail consignment note, freight-forwarder certificate, or carrier delivery evidence
Packing list and serial-number, chassis-number, engine-number, or equipment-identification records for used excavators and rollers
Proof of delivery or import clearance in the destination country where available and commercially appropriate
Accounting records, inventory records, purchase documents, and customer contracts linking each exported machine to the export declaration and invoice
Import VAT and customs documentation for any prior importation where input VAT recovery or customs valuation is relevant
Bank payment evidence or other commercial settlement evidence where needed to corroborate the transaction; an inward-remittance certificate is not a general French statutory export-VAT requirement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France does not impose a general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. Export proceeds should nevertheless be recorded and collected through normal accounting, banking, anti-money-laundering, customs, and transfer-pricing controls. If export exemption or zero-rate treatment is unsupported, the French tax administration may assess the VAT that should have been charged, together with late-payment interest and tax penalties. The principal penalty may be increased for deliberate failure, abuse of law, fraudulent conduct, or concealed activity; the highest fraudulent-evasion penalties can reach 80 percent of the reassessed tax, subject to the applicable statutory classification and procedural safeguards. Input VAT refunds may be denied or clawed back where export evidence is incomplete, inconsistent, fabricated, or not linked to the relevant goods. Customs irregularities may generate customs debt, import VAT reassessment, administrative fines, seizure or forfeiture measures, and potential criminal exposure for serious fraud, false declarations, smuggling, or document falsification. Voluntary correction, contemporaneous evidence preservation, accurate VAT returns, and reconciliation of invoice, inventory, customs, transport, and bank records are required to defend the exemption.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) together with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as the macroprudential and banking supervision arm; Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty exercises residual foreign-exchange licensing powers under the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier, CMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France, as a euro-area member, maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under Regulation (EC) No 1889/2005 and the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union Articles 63-66. The euro is freely convertible for trade, capital movements, and profit remittances. No prior exchange-control approval is required for inbound equity subscriptions, shareholder loans, trade settlement, or dividend repatriation by a non-resident shareholder of a French SAS. Residual restrictions apply exclusively to (i) financial dealings with sanctioned jurisdictions/individuals under EU/UN sanctions, (ii) gold and cash movement declarations above EUR 10,000, and (iii) balance-of-payments statistical reporting to Banque de France for direct investment transactions exceeding EUR 15,000,000 annually or on an ad hoc basis where the counterparty is non-resident. Legal hurdles to profit remittance are negligible, but the bank must receive standard documentary evidence (audited financial statements, tax clearance, UBO declarations) and must file an 'indicateur de la balance des paiements' on the client's behalf.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion of export proceeds applies in France. Export receipts from used construction machinery may be retained in EUR or in any foreign currency account with a licensed credit institution. For foreign-currency accounts, the exporting French entity must comply with the Banque de France monthly reporting threshold (Règlement BCE/ECB 2533/98 and Banque de France instruction) when aggregate external transactions exceed EUR 12,500,000 in one financial year, or immediately for individual operations exceeding EUR 15,000,000. Invoice currency is freely negotiable; however, settlement in USD or non-EUR currencies triggers prudential FX exposure classification and standard 40% risk-weighting under CRR if unhedged. No conversion requirement, no quota, and no export license are imposed for used hydraulic earthmovers (HS 8429.51) provided the goods are not dual-use controlled and civil end-use is declared.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (compte de dépôt professionnel) / Capital Escrow Account (compte séquestre)
Operational Account / Foreign Currency Account (USD, CNY, GBP)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium (conditional). French-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions authorized by ACPR, such as Qonto, Shine, or a foreign EMI passporting under the EEA, can provide multi-currency IBANs, EUR/USD payment accounts, and FX conversion on a software-as-a-service basis. Legal constraints: (i) an EMI does not offer lending, credit, or letter-of-credit issuance, so it cannot replace bank-issued Commercial LC or guarantee products required for trade settlement; (ii) EMI accounts are legally treated as 'fonds de monnaie électronique' and are not eligible as escrow or blocked capital accounts for inbound capital injection where the counterparty requires a true banking guarantee; (iii) EMI AML/KYC does not waive the French obligation to declare UBOs and may require a higher-risk category due to the used-machinery sector; (iv) French banking law forbids an EMI from settling transactions with unlicensed third parties; therefore, any cross-border disbursement must route via a supervised partner bank. Recommended use: operating sub-account and FX conversion, but not as sole repository for Stage 4 capital escrow or LC-backed trade flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is legally permitted under AMF/ACPR guidance for French or EU-licensed entities. For a non-resident shareholder/SAS director, most Tier-1 banks require at least one video-conference interview plus authenticated corporate documents; physical branch presence is still commonly demanded for a non-EU ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) or for opening a Capital Escrow Account. If the director refuses in-person attendance, the bank must enforce an enhanced due diligence (EDD) pathway: notarized apostilled passport copies, sworn translations into French, live video screening with geolocation, and an initial in-person meeting with a French notary or embassy officer. Practical tolerance is 'medium to high requirement'; expect between 4 and 10 weeks for physical or 6 to 8 weeks for remote opening with a full KYC file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Entity type: French SAS newly incorporated or under 12 months of operating history; no audited financial statements; used heavy machinery shell profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kbis extract, Articles of Association, shareholder register, UBO register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) updated within 30 days, notarized proof of capital injection, 3-year business plan with projected machinery inventory and invoice pipeline, scanned contract with an existing supplier/buyer, and sworn affidavit of legitimate commercial purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border used goods and high-value movable assets; potential money-laundering typology of trade over- or under-invoicing and possible shell company fronting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent third-party appraisals (CICBA or similar certified equipment assessment) for each unit, OEM certificate of provenance and serial number registry, prior acquisition invoice with wire trail, customs export declarations (SAD/Douane), Bill of Lading/CMR, pre-shipment inspection certificates, and a signed compliance warranty disclaiming any involvement in organized crime, smuggling, or terrorist financing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident jurisdiction of UBO or shareholder, especially if located outside EU/OECD, raising source-of-funds ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letter from the UBO's home-bank (not older than 3 months), audited annual reports for the shareholder entity, notarized proof of address, personal net-worth statement with tax affidavit, and detailed description of capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.route: shareholder loan agreement if capital remittance is via credit, plus a structured layering rationale explaining each intermediary charge and the final transfer destination.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector association with heavy equipment used in mining/construction, which is a known item in embargoed jurisdictions (e.g., Russia, Iran, Syria) and may trigger dual-use or sanctions screening hits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-user certificate and end-use declaration specifying the exact project site and operator (including GPS coordinates), compliance with Regulation (EU) 833/2014 (Russia-related sanctions) and any CN dual-use checks, list of all intermediary transit countries, technical documentation proving that the machine does not constitute a dual-use controlled item under Reg. 2021/821, and post-sale monitoring commitment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or nominee shareholder arrangements often found in SAS corporate structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full chain-of-ownership from the SAS up to each ultimate individual with percentageholdings, an organizational chart with natural person identification, Statutory Auditor certificate confirming no bearer shares, and a commitment to notify the bank in like kind of any UBO change within 15 days.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity subscription by the non-resident parent must be executed through a licensed bank or an authorized payment institution. Standard rail: SWIFT MT103 for wire transfer in EUR to the SAS's French Operational Account, or a rector 'SPOT' transaction for settlement of foreign currency via TARGET2. The wire must include purpose code 'B016' (direct investment – contribution to capital) or 'B036' (acquisition of equity) under the Banque de France classification, referencing the SAS SIREN number and mandate 'Apport en societe / Capital'. For capital escrow account, the transfer must be made to a blocked 'compte séquestre' at the commercial bank, not an EMI, and the bank will require a notarized Minute of Increase of Capital and, where applicable, an attestation from the Domaines (service de fiscalité). The European Transfer of Funds Regulation (EU) 2015/847 requires full originator and beneficiary information; reject any transfer from an unregulated crypto exchange or anonymous intermediary. The bank will file a Balance of Payments declaration with Banque de France for any direct investment flow; if > EUR 15,000,000, the French entity must submit form 'Enquête fiche mouvement'. No central bank approval is required. To avoid 'reverse hybrid' tax treatment, the share capital should be paid on a bank account of the SAS in France and the bank certificate of deposit attached to the SAS registration dossier.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Preferred rails for trade settlement with overseas suppliers of used construction machinery: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct wire settlement of advance payments or final payment, executed only after verification of supplier's bank details and invoice authenticity; (ii) Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP600, issued by the French bank via SWIFT MT700, confirmed by the beneficiary's bank in the supplier jurisdiction, with MT707 amendment for any change in price/proforma; (iii) Standby Letter of Credit (SBLC) or bank guarantee for performance bonds or after-sales service warranties, using MT760; and (iv) direct debit through SEPA for intra-EU payments in EUR with no FX conversion. For the used construction equipment trade, the recommended structure is a 20% deposit via MT103, 60% against presentation of Bill of Lading and pre-shipment inspection certificate, and 20% after inspection at destination. All outbound wires must include purpose code 'B011' (trade in goods) or 'B007' (services) and the statement 'Déclaration spéciale: rien à déclarer' when below thresholds. For payments to sanctioned countries or where goods could be diverted, an ICC Trade Register-compliant compliance certificate is mandatory. The clearing of LC proceeds may be in EUR or USD; if USD, bank must convert at prevailing interbank rate with a declared spread, and the commercial bank will include the transaction in the CRR large-exposure and FX risk framework.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward (Change à terme) with a licensed French credit institution for EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, or other major counterparties, limited to documentary underlying trade exposure and lasting no longer than 12 months.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for currencies with restricted convertibility (e.g., CNY, INR) permitted only via a French bank acting as principal or through a swap execution facility, with contract referencing an ISDA master agreement or French ABA master agreement, provided the underlying trade receivable/payable is actual and the bank's KYC can prove transactional exposure.
Cross-currency swap (XCCY) as an infrequent risk-management tool, eligible only for larger long-term financing structures and subject to EMIR clearing and margining requirements.
FX options (plain vanillas) strict for hedging of committed commercial flows, not for speculation, and requiring a credit line with the bank.

Commodity-linked hedging instruments are not relevant unless the contract price is pegged to scrap metal indices; if used, they must be bundled into the product margin and disclosed as part of the FX structure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and filing of annual financial statements (dépôt des comptes annuels) comprising balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, annexes, and management report where legally required; the filing may be made in the confidential form if the SAS validly elects that option.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the Guichet unique électronique operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve the accounts within six months of the fiscal-year close, and the approved accounts must be filed with the commercial registry within one month of approval. For a 31 December year-end, approval is due by 30 June and filing by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the SAS to court-ordered injunction and daily penalty payments (astreinte), a criminal fine of up to EUR 9,000, potential loss of capacity to issue receipts and certificates to third parties, and repeated default can lead to administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-ownership declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) on any change in direct or indirect ownership or control; if no change occurs, the declaration is not renewable on a separate annual statutory form but is re-confirmed as part of the annual accounts filing packet.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the Guichet unique; the filing is processed as part of the standard RCS update procedure.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership or control, and in any event before the next annual accounts filing if a change occurred during the fiscal year. There is no separate anniversary filing date for an unchanged UBO structure.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a UBO update can result in criminal fines for the legal entity and its legal representatives, a court-ordered injunction with daily penalty, and refusal by the commercial registry to issue updated Kbis extracts or process further formalities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and supporting schedules (liasse fiscale), including the annual financial statements, tax reconciliation, and transfer-pricing documentation where applicable for cross-border related-party transactions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the electronic filing portal (efile.impots.gouv.fr).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SAS, the return is due by the second working day following 1 May; for a non-calendar fiscal year, the return is due within three months of the fiscal-year close.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a 10% late-filing penalty, reduced to 5% if the assessed tax is settled within 30 days of a formal notice, plus monthly interest of 0.8%; repeated or deliberate failures can lead to additional assessments and publication penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory auditor's report (rapport du commissaire aux comptes) filed together with the annual financial statements when the SAS exceeds the mandatory audit thresholds.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for filing with the annual accounts; copies also submitted to the shareholders' meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The statutory auditor's report must be issued before shareholder approval of the accounts and filed with the RCS within one month of the shareholder approval decision.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a statutory auditor when mandatory, or failure to file the auditor's report with the annual accounts, renders the approval resolution irregular, exposes management to liability, and may lead to nullification of the meeting decisions and fines up to EUR 9,000.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A French SAS must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when, at the end of a fiscal year, it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive fiscal years: total balance-sheet assets exceeding EUR 4,000,000; net turnover exceeding EUR 8,000,000; average workforce exceeding 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory when the SAS controls one or more subsidiaries, employs more than 100 employees, or is required by shareholders holding at least 20% of capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Legal accounts must be prepared under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, ANC regulations); IFRS is permitted only for consolidated group accounts and is not permitted for the individual statutory financial statements of an SAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation declaration. The beneficial-ownership declaration is required at incorporation and must be updated within 30 days of any change in shareholding or control exceeding the 25% threshold. The UBO register must be kept physically at the registered office and kept strictly current; the annual accounts filing procedure provides an administrative cross-check of the registered beneficial ownership data maintained by the RCS.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and share transfer movements (registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of Directors' decisions and related-party agreements (registre des décisions et conventions réglementées)
Minute Book of shareholder meetings and signed written resolutions (procès-verbaux d'assemblées et décisions des associés)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - USD 2,200 per year for a professional registered-office services provider or commercial mailbox service in France
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 - USD 9,000 per year for a standard clean statutory audit of a used heavy-machinery wholesale trading SAS, exclusive of tax and expenses

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: Déclaration de résultats n° 2065-SD (SAS/IS regime) plus annexes n° 2052–2058 series; filed electronically via the DGFiP EFI module 'Espace Professionnel / TéléTVA' (EDI-TDFC or EFI-M) at impots.gouv.fr.
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: Calendar-year entities: file by the second working day of May following year-end (e.g., 4 May for FY ended 31 Dec). Fiscal-year-end evolutions: within three months of the closing date (e.g., FY ended 30 Jun files no later than 30 Sep). The balance-sheet (liasse) must attach accounts, fixed-asset and depreciation tables and the 2016 TP/Master File annex if thresholds are exceeded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2065 – Box 1 / Line 1a ('Résultat fiscal avant imputation des déficits et des crédits d'impôt')
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate net fiscal result after extra-accounting returnees (réintégrations) and dedits (déductions): BIC net income for the used-machinery resale trade, adjusted for non-deductible charges (e.g., fines, excessive directors' remuneration, certain lease-back charges).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident branch of a foreign entity must file the identical 2065 inland for its French permanent establishment (succursale); the result is attributable only if the PE constitutes a ‘exploitation directe’ with fixed place of business and French operational substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report losses carried forward (5-year utilisation under the numeric cap: €1M deductible in full plus 50% of the excess taxable profit; net losses otherwise indefinitely carried forward).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned PE may use losses carried forward only to the extent they are economically linked to French operations, and the PE's books are maintained separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2065 – Box 'Résultat imposable au taux réduit de 15%' (Line 2 / 12)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit eligible for the reduced CIT rate (first €42,500 of net profit) if the SAS meets SME thresholds (≤ 90 employees; turnover/assets ≤ €10M; ≥ 75% beneficial ownership by individuals). Trading profit from used excavator remarketing may be eligible if OECD transparent entities with DTAs are not interposed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A branch of a foreign entity cannot claim the 15% reduced rate for the portion of profits repatriated; the reduced rate applies only to French-law entities themselves.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2065 – Line 'Crédits d'impôt et réductions' (CIR, CICE type credits) / Line 'Quotes' (Contribution sociale sur l'IS)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offsets computed after gross tax (e.g., CIR at 30% of R&D qualifying expenses, foreign-tax credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders only qualify for French tax credits where a DTA contains a matching-credit or vertical-credit provision; the French paying SAS must allocate the right under the treaty residence certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply 25.00% to the standard-rate base, add the 15% reduced-rate tax, then subtract carryback credits and tax credits. Report the final balance of corporate income tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For branches, the branch profit tax (equal to the WHT on deemed dividends) is replaced by the ordinary IS payment if a DTA and articles 214/216 conditions exclude branch-repatriation taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annexes 2056 / 2057 (immobilisations), 2058-A (réintégrations et déductions extra-comptables), 2058-G (transfer pricing & régime de groupe)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detail the acquisition and resale of hydraulic earthmovers: depreciation tables, capital gains of long-term vs short-term classes, intragroup margin reconciliation, and (if threshold met) the local-file & master-file index.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlled transactions (imports of used excavators from foreign affiliates) must be mapped into Annex 2058-G; failure to map triggers the 5% / 1.5% TP sanctions.
